elements.element: Customer has no most-favoured-nation obligation benefiting Vendor.
elements.evidence: Rendered Section 7.2 now reads "Customer has no obligation to disclose or match for Vendor any commercial offer it receives from another provider," eliminating the disclose-and-match obligation; no other provision imposes a most-favoured-customer duty on Customer, and Section 12.3 expressly records that Customer "has made no ... most-favoured-customer ... commitment."

elements.element: The Customer MFN covers only a defined product.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: after the edit no Customer MFN exists at all (7.2 is an express negation), so a product-scope limitation is unnecessary and the element is satisfied vacuously.

elements.element: The Customer MFN lasts no longer than 12 months.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: there is no surviving Customer MFN obligation to which a 12-month sunset could attach; the obligation was removed rather than time-limited.

elements.element: The Customer MFN contains reasonable like-for-like comparison carve-outs.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: with no Customer MFN or match mechanic remaining in 7.2, no comparison carve-outs are needed.

elements.element: The Customer MFN covers only a defined product.
elements.evidence: Not a preferred-level element; assessed at fallback level above.

reasons: Preferred level is complete: the operative disclose-and-match obligation in Section 7.2 has been replaced with an express statement that Customer owes no such obligation, so no MFN runs in Vendor's favour.

The edit is confined to the single offending sentence in Section 7.2; the remaining fee provisions and Section 12.3 are untouched, and no extras (survival tails, procedures, damages categories, or added requirements) were introduced.

Intent is preserved and an internal inconsistency is cured: the revised 7.2 now aligns with Section 12.3's acknowledgement that Customer made no most-favoured-customer commitment; no undefined terms or dangling cross-references result.

Fallback elements are satisfied only vacuously because the obligation was deleted rather than narrowed; the operative position rests on the preferred level, which is the correct outcome under the direction rule (Vendor-granted MFN pricing in Customer's favour, if any, is unaffected).

Note for the drafter: retaining an affirmative negation ('Customer has no obligation to disclose or match...') rather than striking 7.2 entirely leaves a numbered clause with no operative burden; this is acceptable and arguably clearer, but a straight deletion would be equally compliant if renumbering is not a concern.
